newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Lyonnaise des Eaux to expand in Cambodia, SE Asia.
newsitem.headline: Lyonnaise des Eaux to expand in Cambodia, SE Asia.

text.p: The chief of France's Lyonnaise des Eaux SA industrial group said on Friday his firm would focus on infrastructure development in southeast Asia, including possibly developing Cambodia's most famous tourist destination.
"We think Southeast Asia is really the spot," said Jerome Monod, president and director general of Lyonnaise des Eaux, one of France's top 20 companies.
He said his company would invest as much as 200 million to 300 million francs ($36 million to $54 million) equity in Cambodia in the next five years.

In Cambodia, one of its subsidiaries is part of a consortium managing and expanding Pochentong International Airport at a cost of $100 million and has completed two upgrades to the country's decrepit water treatment and distribution system.
Lyonnaise des Eaux would also dredge parts of the Mekong River and deepen and enlarge the southern port of Sihanoukville, Monod told reporters.
On the drawing board was a plan to manage the country's famous temples at Angkor and joint hotel ventures there through the subsidiary Culture Espace, Monod said.
"We are interested in hotels, in what we know -- which is environmental services, especially water. We are interested in investing in the long term," he noted.

Lyonnaise's subsidiary Dumez GTM Cambodge bid to manage and develop the historic Angkor site last year along with at least six other firms, but controversy erupted when tourism officials insisted the site had already been awarded to Malaysia's YTL Ltd Bhd in November 1995.
YTL wants to build a hotel zone and create a $20 million sound and light show at the temples, a plan that Apsara, the government agency that oversees the site, has questioned.
"It would be a disaster to do Disneyland there," Monod said.

He maintained that rights to the site remained up for grabs and he was optimistic about playing a part in a development consortium there after meeting King Norodom Sihanouk and co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen.
